The lower shrine is the [[Honden]] and is a ''[[Shinmei-zukuri]]'' structure with a cypress bark roof. It was rebuilt in 1845 and is designated as a Tangible Cultural Property of Kyoto Prefecture{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} During the [[Meiji period]] era of [[State Shinto]], the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 2nd Rank |国幣中社|[[kokuhei-chūsha]]}} under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines]]Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. (1959). ''The Imperial House of Japan,'' pp. 125. The shrine is located next to the [[Amanohashidate]]. ==Cultural Properties== ===NationalTreasures=== *{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図||}}, early [[Heian period]], it is considered the oldest family tree in Japan.The clan claims descent from Amenohoakari, and served as at the ''[[kuni no miyatsuko]]'' of [[Tanba Province]] before it was divided into Tamba and Tango.The document records 82 generations of descent from Amenohoakari. It was designated a National Treasure in 1972.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777|title=海部氏系図|trans-title=Amebe shikeizu|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 20, 2020}} ===National Important Cultural Properties=== *'''{{nihongo|Biane'''|扁額}}, wooden, [[Heian period]], inscribed "Kago no Daimyōjin", dated 976.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/5326|title=木造扁額|trans-title=Mokuzō hengaku|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 20, 2020}} *'''{{nihongo|[[Komainu]]'''|狛犬||}}, stone, [[Momoyama period]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/3741|title=石造狛犬|trans-title=Sekizōkomainu|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 20, 2020}} * '''{{nihongo|Excavated Items from Kono Jinja Kyozuka|丹後国府中籠神社経塚出土品|}}''', [[Heian period]], consisting of two copper cylinders, one mirror with a design of chrysanthemum, and mirror with a line drawing of a Buddha, dated 1188{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/9835|title=丹後国府中籠神社経塚出土品|trans-title=Tango kuni Fuchū kojinja Kyōdzuka shutsudo-hin|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 20, 2020}} ==Gallery== File:Kono-jinja (Miyazu) honden.JPG|Honden（Kyoto Prefectural ICP） File:Kono-jinja Miyazu3.JPG|Yamato ''Sazare-ishi'' File:Kono-jinja Miyazu Kyoto Pref04n3000.jpg|Koma-inu（ICP） File:Kono-jinja Miyazu Kyoto Pref05n3000.jpg|Koma-inu（ICP） File:Kono-jinja (Miyazu) shinmon.JPG|Gate File:Kono-jinja (Miyazu) torii.JPG|Ni-no-Torii ==See also== *[[List of Shinto shrines]] *[[List of National Treasures of Japan (ancient documents)]] *[[Ichinomiya]] {{神社 |名称 = {{ill|Kago Shrine|ja|籠神社|qq=draft}} |image = [[File:Kono-jinja (Miyazu) haiden.JPG|270px]]

{{ill|Betsuhyō Jinja|ja|別表神社|1=Beppyo Shrine|2=ja|3=別表神社|4=simple|5=Beppyo shrine|6=zh|7=別表神社|8=mr|9=बेप्प्यो तीर्थ|qq=draft}} |創建 = Unknown (pre-history) |本殿 = {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|qq=draft}} |別名 = {{ill|Moto-Ise Kago Shrine|ja|元伊勢籠神社|qq=draft}}・{{ill|Naiku Moto-Miya|ja|内宮元宮|qq=draft}}・{{ill|Komori Daikongen|ja|籠守大権現|qq=draft}} |札所等 = {{ill|Shinbutsu Reijōjunpai no Michi|ja|神仏霊場巡拝の道|qq=draft}} No. 131 (Kyoto No. 51) |例祭 = {{ill|April 24 (Aoi-sai)|ja|4月24日（葵祭）|qq=draft}} |神事 = |地図 = {{Location map|Japan Kyoto|label={{ill|Kago Shrine|ja|籠神社|qq=draft}}|position=top|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}}{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} {{GeoGroup}} [[File:Precincts of Kono-jinja.JPG|thumb|{{center|View of the precincts (from {{ill|Kasamatsu Park|ja|傘松公園|qq=draft}})}}{{small|Shrine buildings visible at lower left, and {{ill|Amanohashidate|ja|天橋立|qq=draft}} at upper right.}}]] [[File:Kono-jinja (Miyazu) otorii.JPG|thumb|{{center|First Torii}}]] '''Kago Shrine''' (read “Kono-jinja” – also sometimes read “Komori-jinja,” though the reading “Kono-jinja” is used here) is a Shinto shrine located in Ōgaki, [[Miyazu City]], [[Kyoto Prefecture]]. It is classified as a Shikinai Taisha (Meishin Taisha) and the Ichinomiya of Tango Province. Its former shrine Ranking under the modern system was that of a Kokuhēchūsha, and it is now one of the Betsuhyō Jinja under the Association of Shinto Shrines. It is also one of the shrines of Moto-Ise, and is known by various names such as “Moto-Ise Kago Shrine,” “Naiku Moto-Miya,” “Komori Daikongen,” and “Kago Daimyōjin.” The shrine’s head priest has been hereditary in the {{ill|Amabe Clan|ja|海部氏|qq=draft}}. Although the origin of the Sōsha of Tango Province is unknown, one theory holds that this shrine also served as the Sōsha. In April 2017 (Heisei 29), the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology recognized it as one of the cultural properties that help tell the story of Japan’s cultural heritage – as part of the “Japan Heritage” story "Tango Chirimen Corridor."{{Cite web|和書|author=文化庁|authorlink=文化庁|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/nihon_isan/pdf/nihon_isan_pamphlet_2019.pdf|title=日本遺産認定ストーリー一覧|accessdate=2020-11-11}}{{Cite web|和書|author=文化庁|authorlink=文化庁|url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story043/index.html|title=300th year を紡ぐ絹が織り成す丹後ちりめん回廊|website=日本遺産ポータルサイト|accessdate=2020-11-11}} == Enshrined Deities == The deities enshrined at Kago Shrine consist of five figures. '''Principal Deity''' * '''{{ill|Hikoakitsumeri no Mikoto|ja|彦火明命|qq=draft}}''' (Hikoakitsumeri no Mikoto) **Also referred to as {{ill|Amatenohikohikari no Mikoto|ja|天火明命|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Amaterasu Mitama no Kami|ja|天照御魂神|qq=draft}}, or {{ill|Amaterasu Kuniteru Hikoakitsumeri no Mikoto|ja|天照国照彦火明命|qq=draft}}, as well as {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft}}; considered the ancestral deity of the Amabe clan. '''Associated Deities''' * {{ill|Toyouke-no-Ōkami|ja|豊受大神|lt=Toyouke Ōmikami|1=Toyouke-hime|qq=draft}} – also known as “Goshizunushi,” * {{ill|Amaterasu-Ōkami|ja|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Watatsumi|ja|海神|qq=draft}} – the tutelary deity of the Amabe clan. * {{ill|Ame-no-Mikumari no Kami|ja|天水分神|qq=draft}} Various theories exist regarding these enshrined deities.{{ill|Japanese Deities|ja|日本の神々|1=Kamigami|qq=draft}} – Kago Shrine entry. According to the "Tango-koku Shikishōjō Jikkō," {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|qq=draft}} is cited,Based on a tradition from an excerpt of the "Tango-koku Fudoki" (as included in the Shaku Nihonki). while the "Shinja Meisaichō" lists Ame-no-Mikumari as the deity. == History == Kago Shrine was founded in the 3rd year of {{ill|Shinkame|ja|神亀|qq=draft}} (726) during the Nara period. According to shrine tradition, the site is the place where {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|qq=draft}} temporarily stayed on her return journey from the conquest of the Three Kingdoms. According to the "Hakozaki Shrine Engi" (a record from {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|ja|石清水八幡宮|qq=draft}}), in the 21st year of {{ill|Engi|ja|延喜|qq=draft}} (921) an oracle was received regarding the relocation to Hakozaki-hama (the present-day Hakozaki area of Higashi Ward in [[Fukuoka City]]); then in the 1st year of {{ill|Enchō|ja|延長|qq=draft}} (923) the shrine was relocated, marking the beginning of Hakozaki Shrine. The oracle for Hakozaki Shrine was drawn from the oracle collection of Usa Jingu, the origin story of the Hachiman deities, which states, "Either I, from Usa Jingu, or the Hon-miya of Honami Oita is my main shrine." Even after relocating to Hakozaki Shrine, it continued to be fervently venerated as the head branch (第一社) among the Five Hachiman Shrines of Kyushu. Nearby, there are ruins of an ancient temple and the remains of the "Daibu Haiji" pagoda. At the time of its founding, the shrine buildings were located on a hillside behind the present site, but during the Sengoku period they were burned down in warfare. In the 5th year of {{ill|Tenshō|ja|天正|1=Tenshō (Momoyama period)|lt=Tenshō Era|qq=draft}} (1577), {{ill|Akizuki Tanemi|ja|秋月種実|qq=draft}} rebuilt the shrine at the current location. In 1872 (Meiji 5), it was classified as a Gōsha under the modern shrine Ranking system. In 1995 (Heisei 7), a major restoration was carried out. == Facilities == [[File:Pond in Daibu Hachiman Shrine.jpg|thumb|250px|Hojo Pond]] [[File:Grand camphor tree in Daibu Hachiman Shrine.jpg|thumb|250px|Great Camphor Tree]] * Haiden (Worship Hall) * Honden (Main Hall) **Both the Haiden and Honden were extensively repaired in Heisei 7 (1995). * Shimon (Divine Gate) * Hojo Pond – a pond used during the Hojo Festival. * The Well of Emperor Ōjin’s Birth Water * Great Camphor Tree – an estimated 350‑year‑old camphor tree ({{ill|Kusunoki|ja|クスノキ|qq=draft}}) designated as a Natural Monument of Fukuoka Prefecture. According to tradition, it is said to be a descendant of the tree that {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|qq=draft}} brought back from the Korean Peninsula. * Uguisuzuka – a hill approximately 10 meters high located on a detached part of the grounds near [[Chikuzen Oita Station]] on JR; according to tradition, Empress Jingū disbanded her troops here, and it is said that the place name “Oita” originated from this event. == Annual Festival == At the annual festival (Hojo-kai) held each September, the “Daibu Lion Dance” is performed. This lion dance is designated as an Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Fukuoka Prefecture. It is said to have been transmitted from {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|ja|石清水八幡宮|qq=draft}} during the Edo period (specifically in Kyōhō 9, 1724) and, together with the “Earth-worker Lion Dance” from Hakata (in {{ill|Kaho District|ja|嘉穂郡|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Katsugawa Town|ja|桂川町|qq=draft}}), has influenced lion dances in southern Fukuoka. It is also noted that, perhaps due to transmission from Kyoto, the accompanying festival music and shouts have a nuance similar to Kyoto dialect. == Access == * Approximately a 15‑minute walk from [[JR Kyushu]]’s {{ill|Fukuhoku Yutaka Line|ja|福北ゆたか線|qq=draft}} [[Chikuzen Oita Station|Chikuzen Oita Station]]. == External Links == * [http://www.daibu-hachiman.com/ 【公式】{{ill|Daibu Hachiman-gu|ja|大分八幡宮}]] * [http://www.kankou-iizuka.jp/homepage/sub.asp?id=90 【Daibu Hachiman-gu】 (Iizuka City website)] {{shinto-stub}} {{Normdaten}} ==Overview== ==References== * Plutschow, Herbe. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on April 24.The shrine is also called the {{nihongo|'''Moto-Ise Kono Jinja'''|元伊勢籠神社}}, and its ''[[kannushi]]'' has been in the Amabe clan since the [[Kofun period]].{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} It may be the [[Sōja shrine]] and [[Ichinomiya]] of the [[Tango Province]] ==Enshrined ''kami''== The primary ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Kono Jinja is: * {{nihongo|'''[[Amenohoakari]]'''|彦火明命 |}}, god of the sun and agriculture The secondary ''kami'' are: * {{nihongo|'''[[Toyoukebime]]'''|豊受大神|lt=Toyouke Ōmikami|1=Toyouke-hime}}, goddess of agriculture and industry * {{nihongo|'''[[Amaterasu]]'''|天照大神}}, goddess of the sun * {{nihongo|'''[[Watatsumi]]'''|海神}}, water deity * {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Ame-no-mikumari-no-kami|lt=Mikumari-no-Kami|sv|Mikumari-no-Kami|qq=draft}}'''|天水分神}} ==History== According to the legend of this shrine, Toyouke-Ōmikami was originally enshrined that this location before being relocated to the Outer Shrine of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]] during the reign of [[Emperor Yūryaku]] to offer sacred food to [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu Ōmikami]], the Sun Goddess. The shrine was originally called the {{nihongo|Manai Jinja|真名井神社||}}, but was renamed in 671 by the 26th generation ''kannushi'' to "Kagomiya" or "Kago Jinja" based on the tradition that the god of worship appeared in the snow in a basket. The main ''kami'' enshrined was changed to Amenohoakari in 719 by the 27th generation ''kannushi'', but Toyouke-Ōmikami retained as a secondary object of worship.The shrine and its rituals are described in both the ''[[Kojiki]]'' and the ''[[Nihon Shoki]]''. The shrine is listed in the ''[[Engishiki]]'' records from the early [[Heian period]], as a {{nihongo|''Myōjin Taisha''|名神大社||}} and the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of the province. The lower shrine is the [[Honden]] and is a ''[[Shinmei-zukuri]]'' structure with a cypress bark roof. It was rebuilt in 1845 and is designated as a Tangible Cultural Property of Kyoto Prefecture{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} During the [[Meiji period]] era of [[State Shinto]], the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 2nd Rank |国幣中社|[[kokuhei-chūsha]]}} under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines]]Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. It is classified as a Shikinai Taisha (Meishin Taisha) and the Ichinomiya of Tango Province. Its former shrine Ranking under the modern system was that of a Kokuhēchūsha, and it is now one of the Betsuhyō Jinja under the Association of Shinto Shrines. It is also one of the shrines of Moto-Ise, and is known by various names such as “Moto-Ise Kago Shrine,” “Naiku Moto-Miya,” “Komori Daikongen,” and “Kago Daimyōjin.” The shrine’s head priest has been hereditary in the {{ill|Amabe Clan|ja|海部氏|qq=draft}}. Although the origin of the Sōsha of Tango Province is unknown, one theory holds that this shrine also served as the Sōsha. In April 2017 (Heisei 29), the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology recognized it as one of the cultural properties that help tell the story of Japan’s cultural heritage – as part of the “Japan Heritage” story "Tango Chirimen Corridor."{{Cite web|和書|author=文化庁|authorlink=文化庁|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/nihon_isan/pdf/nihon_isan_pamphlet_2019.pdf|title=日本遺産認定ストーリー一覧|accessdate=2020-11-11}}{{Cite web|和書|author=文化庁|authorlink=文化庁|url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story043/index.html|title=300th year を紡ぐ絹が織り成す丹後ちりめん回廊|website=日本遺産ポータルサイト|accessdate=2020-11-11}} == Enshrined Deities == The deities enshrined at Kago Shrine consist of five figures. '''Principal Deity''' * '''{{ill|Hikoakitsumeri no Mikoto|ja|彦火明命|qq=draft}}''' (Hikoakitsumeri no Mikoto) **Also referred to as {{ill|Amatenohikohikari no Mikoto|ja|天火明命|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Amaterasu Mitama no Kami|ja|天照御魂神|qq=draft}}, or {{ill|Amaterasu Kuniteru Hikoakitsumeri no Mikoto|ja|天照国照彦火明命|qq=draft}}, as well as {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft}}; considered the ancestral deity of the Amabe clan. '''Associated Deities''' * {{ill|Toyouke-no-Ōkami|ja|豊受大神|lt=Toyouke Ōmikami|1=Toyouke-hime|qq=draft}} – also known as “Goshizunushi,” * {{ill|Amaterasu-Ōkami|ja|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Watatsumi|ja|海神|qq=draft}} – the tutelary deity of the Amabe clan. * {{ill|Ame-no-Mikumari no Kami|ja|天水分神|qq=draft}} Various theories exist regarding these enshrined deities.{{ill|Japanese Deities|ja|日本の神々|1=Kamigami|qq=draft}} – Kago Shrine entry. According to the "Tango-koku Shikishōjō Jikkō," {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|qq=draft}} is cited,Based on a tradition from an excerpt of the "Tango-koku Fudoki" (as included in the Shaku Nihonki). while the "Shinja Meisaichō" lists Ame-no-Mikumari as the deity. == History == Kago Shrine was founded in the 3rd year of {{ill|Shinkame|ja|神亀|qq=draft}} (726) during the Nara period. According to shrine tradition, the site is the place where {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|qq=draft}} temporarily stayed on her return journey from the conquest of the Three Kingdoms. According to the "Hakozaki Shrine Engi" (a record from {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|ja|石清水八幡宮|qq=draft}}), in the 21st year of {{ill|Engi|ja|延喜|qq=draft}} (921) an oracle was received regarding the relocation to Hakozaki-hama (the present-day Hakozaki area of Higashi Ward in [[Fukuoka City]]); then in the 1st year of {{ill|Enchō|ja|延長|qq=draft}} (923) the shrine was relocated, marking the beginning of Hakozaki Shrine. The oracle for Hakozaki Shrine was drawn from the oracle collection of Usa Jingu, the origin story of the Hachiman deities, which states, "Either I, from Usa Jingu, or the Hon-miya of Honami Oita is my main shrine." Even after relocating to Hakozaki Shrine, it continued to be fervently venerated as the head branch (第一社) among the Five Hachiman Shrines of Kyushu. Nearby, there are ruins of an ancient temple and the remains of the "Daibu Haiji" pagoda. At the time of its founding, the shrine buildings were located on a hillside behind the present site, but during the Sengoku period they were burned down in warfare. In the 5th year of {{ill|Tenshō|ja|天正|1=Tenshō (Momoyama period)|lt=Tenshō Era|qq=draft}} (1577), {{ill|Akizuki Tanemi|ja|秋月種実|qq=draft}} rebuilt the shrine at the current location. In 1872 (Meiji 5), it was classified as a Gōsha under the modern shrine Ranking system. In 1995 (Heisei 7), a major restoration was carried out. == Facilities == [[File:Pond in Daibu Hachiman Shrine.jpg|thumb|250px|Hojo Pond]] [[File:Grand camphor tree in Daibu Hachiman Shrine.jpg|thumb|250px|Great Camphor Tree]] * Haiden (Worship Hall) * Honden (Main Hall) **Both the Haiden and Honden were extensively repaired in Heisei 7 (1995). * Shimon (Divine Gate) * Hojo Pond – a pond used during the Hojo Festival. * The Well of Emperor Ōjin’s Birth Water * Great Camphor Tree – an estimated 350‑year‑old camphor tree ({{ill|Kusunoki|ja|クスノキ|qq=draft}}) designated as a Natural Monument of Fukuoka Prefecture. According to tradition, it is said to be a descendant of the tree that {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|qq=draft}} brought back from the Korean Peninsula. * Uguisuzuka – a hill approximately 10 meters high located on a detached part of the grounds near [[Chikuzen Oita Station]] on JR; according to tradition, Empress Jingū disbanded her troops here, and it is said that the place name “Oita” originated from this event. == Annual Festival == At the annual festival (Hojo-kai) held each September, the “Daibu Lion Dance” is performed. This lion dance is designated as an Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Fukuoka Prefecture. It is said to have been transmitted from {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|ja|石清水八幡宮|qq=draft}} during the Edo period (specifically in Kyōhō 9, 1724) and, together with the “Earth-worker Lion Dance” from Hakata (in {{ill|Kaho District|ja|嘉穂郡|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Katsugawa Town|ja|桂川町|qq=draft}}), has influenced lion dances in southern Fukuoka. It is also noted that, perhaps due to transmission from Kyoto, the accompanying festival music and shouts have a nuance similar to Kyoto dialect. == Access == * Approximately a 15‑minute walk from [[JR Kyushu]]’s {{ill|Fukuhoku Yutaka Line|ja|福北ゆたか線|qq=draft}} [[Chikuzen Oita Station|Chikuzen Oita Station]]. == External Links == * [http://www.daibu-hachiman.com/ 【公式】{{ill|Daibu Hachiman-gu|ja|大分八幡宮}]] * [http://www.kankou-iizuka.jp/homepage/sub.asp?id=90 【Daibu Hachiman-gu】 (Iizuka City website)] {{shinto-stub}} {{Normdaten}} ==Overview== ==References== * Plutschow, Herbe. ''Matsuri: The Festivals of Japan''. RoutledgeCurzon (1996) {{ISBN|1-873410-63-8}} * [[Richard Ponsonby-Fane|Ponsonby-Fane]], Richard Arthur Brabazon. (1959). [https://books.google.com/books?id=SLAeAAAAMAAJ&q=The+Imperial+House+of+Japan ''The Imperial House of Japan.''] Kyoto: Ponsonby Memorial Society. [http://www.worldcat.org/wcpa/oclc/194887 OCLC 194887] ==External links== {{commons category|Kono-jinja (Miyazu)}} *[https://www.motoise.jp Official home page] ==Notes== {{reflist}} {{Shinto shrine}} {{Munakata Faith}} {{Shinmei shrines}} {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ {{Ichinomiya}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages to be reviewed for curly bracket replacement error]] [[Category:Shrines in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Miyazu City]] [[Category:History of Miyazu City]] [[Category:Meishin Taisha]] [[Category:Shikinai Taisha of Tango Province|名このしんしや]] [[Category:Ichinomiya]] [[Category:Kokuhēchūsha]] [[Category:National Treasures of Japan (Calligraphy, Documents, and Ancient Manuscripts)]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:Moto-Ise]] [[Category:Shinsei Taisha|社1]] [[Category:Japan Heritage]] [[Category:Pages that used to use Authority control]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Tango Province]] [[Category:Miyazu, Kyoto]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:National Treasures of Japan]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:beppyo shinmei shrines needed to be moved in template]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Moto-Ise shrines]] [[Category:Pages goodbye $1 Wikipedia 8]] [[Category:Kono Shrine]] [[Category:Moto-Geku Shrines]] [[Category:Munakata Faith]] [[Category:Expanded pages from Wikipedia]] }} [[sn:Kono Shrine]] [[en:Kono Shrine]] [[sn:ono Shrine]] [[sn: failed]]

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Kyoto Prefecture, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Kono Jinja
籠神社 | image = Kono-jinja (Miyazu) haiden.JPG | caption = Haiden of Kono Jinja {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Kyoto Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|34|58.13|N|135|11|48.01|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Amenohoakari]] | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location =430 Ōgaki, Miyazu-shi, Kyoto-fu 629-2242 | website = {{Official|1=https://www.motoise.jp}} | architecture_style = ''Shinmei-zukuri'' | festival = April 24 | leadership = | designation1 = National Treasure of Japan | footnotes ={{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=pink|text align=center|[[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|Important Cultural Property]]}} }} [[File:Amabe Clan genealogy.jpg|right|thumb|Amabe clan genealogy]] {{nihongo|'''Kono Jinja'''|籠神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] in the Ōgaki neighborhood of the city of [[Miyazu, Kyoto|Miyazu]] in [[Kyoto Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of former [[Tango Province]]. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on April 24.The shrine is also called the {{nihongo|'''Moto-Ise Kono Jinja'''|元伊勢籠神社}}, and its ''[[kannushi]]'' has been in the Amabe clan since the [[Kofun period]].{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} It may be the [[Sōja shrine]] and [[Ichinomiya]] of the [[Tango Province]] ==Enshrined ''kami''== The primary ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Kono Jinja is: * {{nihongo|'''[[Amenohoakari]]'''|彦火明命 |}}, god of the sun and agriculture The secondary ''kami'' are: * {{nihongo|'''[[Toyoukebime]]'''|豊受大神|lt=Toyouke Ōmikami|1=Toyouke-hime}}, goddess of agriculture and industry * {{nihongo|'''[[Amaterasu]]'''|天照大神}}, goddess of the sun * {{nihongo|'''[[Watatsumi]]'''|海神}}, water deity * {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Ame-no-mikumari-no-kami|lt=Mikumari-no-Kami|sv|Mikumari-no-Kami|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-mikumari-no-kami|qq=}}'''|天水分神}} ==History== According to the legend of this shrine, Toyouke-Ōmikami was originally enshrined that this location before being relocated to the Outer Shrine of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]] during the reign of [[Emperor Yūryaku]] to offer sacred food to [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu Ōmikami]], the Sun Goddess. The shrine was originally called the {{nihongo|Manai Jinja|真名井神社||}}, but was renamed in 671 by the 26th generation ''kannushi'' to "Kagomiya" or "Kago Jinja" based on the tradition that the god of worship appeared in the snow in a basket. The main ''kami'' enshrined was changed to Amenohoakari in 719 by the 27th generation ''kannushi'', but Toyouke-Ōmikami retained as a secondary object of worship.The shrine and its rituals are described in both the ''[[Kojiki]]'' and the ''[[Nihon Shoki]]''. The shrine is listed in the ''[[Engishiki]]'' records from the early [[Heian period]], as a {{nihongo|''Myōjin Taisha''|名神大社||}} and the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of the province. It was located immediately to the west of the site of the Tango [[kokufu|provincial capital]].{{cite book |last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese}} The shrine consists of an upper and lower portion. The lower shrine is the [[Honden]] and is a ''[[Shinmei-zukuri]]'' structure with a cypress bark roof. It was rebuilt in 1845 and is designated as a Tangible Cultural Property of Kyoto Prefecture{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} During the [[Meiji period]] era of [[State Shinto]], the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 2nd Rank |国幣中社|[[kokuhei-chūsha]]}} under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines]]Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. (1959). ''The Imperial House of Japan,'' pp. 125. The shrine is located next to the [[Amanohashidate]]. ==Cultural Properties== ===NationalTreasures=== *{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図||}}, early [[Heian period]], it is considered the oldest family tree in Japan.The clan claims descent from Amenohoakari, and served as at the ''[[kuni no miyatsuko]]'' of [[Tanba Province]] before it was divided into Tamba and Tango.The document records 82 generations of descent from Amenohoakari. It was designated a National Treasure in 1972.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777|title=海部氏系図|trans-title=Amebe shikeizu|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 20, 2020}} ===National Important Cultural Properties=== *'''{{nihongo|Biane'''|扁額}}, wooden, [[Heian period]], inscribed "Kago no Daimyōjin", dated 976.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/5326|title=木造扁額|trans-title=Mokuzō hengaku|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 20, 2020}} *'''{{nihongo|[[Komainu]]'''|狛犬||}}, stone, [[Momoyama period]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/3741|title=石造狛犬|trans-title=Sekizōkomainu|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 20, 2020}} * '''{{nihongo|Excavated Items from Kono Jinja Kyozuka|丹後国府中籠神社経塚出土品|}}''', [[Heian period]], consisting of two copper cylinders, one mirror with a design of chrysanthemum, and mirror with a line drawing of a Buddha, dated 1188{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/9835|title=丹後国府中籠神社経塚出土品|trans-title=Tango kuni Fuchū kojinja Kyōdzuka shutsudo-hin|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 20, 2020}} ==Gallery== File:Kono-jinja (Miyazu) honden.JPG|Honden（Kyoto Prefectural ICP） File:Kono-jinja Miyazu3.JPG|Yamato ''Sazare-ishi'' File:Kono-jinja Miyazu Kyoto Pref04n3000.jpg|Koma-inu（ICP） File:Kono-jinja Miyazu Kyoto Pref05n3000.jpg|Koma-inu（ICP） File:Kono-jinja (Miyazu) shinmon.JPG|Gate File:Kono-jinja (Miyazu) torii.JPG|Ni-no-Torii ==See also== *[[List of Shinto shrines]] *[[List of National Treasures of Japan (ancient documents)]] *[[Ichinomiya]] {{神社 |名称 = {{ill|Kago Shrine|ja|籠神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kago Shrine|qq=}} |image = [[File:Kono-jinja (Miyazu) haiden.JPG|270px]]

In April 2017 (Heisei 29), the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology recognized it as one of the cultural properties that help tell the story of Japan’s cultural heritage – as part of the “Japan Heritage” story "Tango Chirimen Corridor."{{Cite web|和書|author=文化庁|authorlink=文化庁|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/nihon_isan/pdf/nihon_isan_pamphlet_2019.pdf|title=日本遺産認定ストーリー一覧|accessdate=2020-11-11}}{{Cite web|和書|author=文化庁|authorlink=文化庁|url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story043/index.html|title=300th year を紡ぐ絹が織り成す丹後ちりめん回廊|website=日本遺産ポータルサイト|accessdate=2020-11-11}} == Enshrined Deities == The deities enshrined at Kago Shrine consist of five figures. '''Principal Deity''' * '''{{ill|Hikoakitsumeri no Mikoto|ja|彦火明命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hikoakitsumeri no Mikoto|qq=}}''' (Hikoakitsumeri no Mikoto) **Also referred to as {{ill|Amatenohikohikari no Mikoto|ja|天火明命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amatenohikohikari no Mikoto|qq=}}, {{ill|Amaterasu Mitama no Kami|ja|天照御魂神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Mitama no Kami|qq=}}, or {{ill|Amaterasu Kuniteru Hikoakitsumeri no Mikoto|ja|天照国照彦火明命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Kuniteru Hikoakitsumeri no Mikoto|qq=}}, as well as {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=}}; considered the ancestral deity of the Amabe clan. '''Associated Deities''' * {{ill|Toyouke-no-Ōkami|ja|豊受大神|lt=Toyouke Ōmikami|1=Toyouke-hime|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke-no-Ōkami|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke-hime|qq=}} – also known as “Goshizunushi,” * {{ill|Amaterasu-Ōkami|ja|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu-Ōkami|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}} * {{ill|Watatsumi|ja|海神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Watatsumi|qq=}} – the tutelary deity of the Amabe clan. * {{ill|Ame-no-Mikumari no Kami|ja|天水分神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Mikumari no Kami|qq=}} Various theories exist regarding these enshrined deities.{{ill|Japanese Deities|ja|日本の神々|1=Kamigami|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Deities|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamigami|qq=}} – Kago Shrine entry. According to the "Tango-koku Shikishōjō Jikkō," {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qq=}} is cited,Based on a tradition from an excerpt of the "Tango-koku Fudoki" (as included in the Shaku Nihonki). while the "Shinja Meisaichō" lists Ame-no-Mikumari as the deity. == History == Kago Shrine was founded in the 3rd year of {{ill|Shinkame|ja|神亀|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinkame|qq=}} (726) during the Nara period. According to shrine tradition, the site is the place where {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Empress Jingū|qq=}} temporarily stayed on her return journey from the conquest of the Three Kingdoms. According to the "Hakozaki Shrine Engi" (a record from {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|ja|石清水八幡宮|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwashimizu Hachimangū|qq=}}), in the 21st year of {{ill|Engi|ja|延喜|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi|qq=}} (921) an oracle was received regarding the relocation to Hakozaki-hama (the present-day Hakozaki area of Higashi Ward in [[Fukuoka City]]); then in the 1st year of {{ill|Enchō|ja|延長|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enchō|qq=}} (923) the shrine was relocated, marking the beginning of Hakozaki Shrine. The oracle for Hakozaki Shrine was drawn from the oracle collection of Usa Jingu, the origin story of the Hachiman deities, which states, "Either I, from Usa Jingu, or the Hon-miya of Honami Oita is my main shrine." Even after relocating to Hakozaki Shrine, it continued to be fervently venerated as the head branch (第一社) among the Five Hachiman Shrines of Kyushu. Nearby, there are ruins of an ancient temple and the remains of the "Daibu Haiji" pagoda. At the time of its founding, the shrine buildings were located on a hillside behind the present site, but during the Sengoku period they were burned down in warfare. In the 5th year of {{ill|Tenshō|ja|天正|1=Tenshō (Momoyama period)|lt=Tenshō Era|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenshō|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenshō (Momoyama period)|qq=}} (1577), {{ill|Akizuki Tanemi|ja|秋月種実|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akizuki Tanemi|qq=}} rebuilt the shrine at the current location. In 1872 (Meiji 5), it was classified as a Gōsha under the modern shrine Ranking system. In 1995 (Heisei 7), a major restoration was carried out. == Facilities == [[File:Pond in Daibu Hachiman Shrine.jpg|thumb|250px|Hojo Pond]] [[File:Grand camphor tree in Daibu Hachiman Shrine.jpg|thumb|250px|Great Camphor Tree]] * Haiden (Worship Hall) * Honden (Main Hall) **Both the Haiden and Honden were extensively repaired in Heisei 7 (1995). * Shimon (Divine Gate) * Hojo Pond – a pond used during the Hojo Festival. * The Well of Emperor Ōjin’s Birth Water * Great Camphor Tree – an estimated 350‑year‑old camphor tree ({{ill|Kusunoki|ja|クスノキ|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki|qq=}}) designated as a Natural Monument of Fukuoka Prefecture. According to tradition, it is said to be a descendant of the tree that {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Empress Jingū|qq=}} brought back from the Korean Peninsula. * Uguisuzuka – a hill approximately 10 meters high located on a detached part of the grounds near [[Chikuzen Oita Station]] on JR; according to tradition, Empress Jingū disbanded her troops here, and it is said that the place name “Oita” originated from this event. == Annual Festival == At the annual festival (Hojo-kai) held each September, the “Daibu Lion Dance” is performed. This lion dance is designated as an Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Fukuoka Prefecture. It is said to have been transmitted from {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|ja|石清水八幡宮|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwashimizu Hachimangū|qq=}} during the Edo period (specifically in Kyōhō 9, 1724) and, together with the “Earth-worker Lion Dance” from Hakata (in {{ill|Kaho District|ja|嘉穂郡|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaho District|qq=}}, {{ill|Katsugawa Town|ja|桂川町|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katsugawa Town|qq=}}), has influenced lion dances in southern Fukuoka. It is also noted that, perhaps due to transmission from Kyoto, the accompanying festival music and shouts have a nuance similar to Kyoto dialect. == Access == * Approximately a 15‑minute walk from [[JR Kyushu]]’s {{ill|Fukuhoku Yutaka Line|ja|福北ゆたか線|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuhoku Yutaka Line|qq=}} [[Chikuzen Oita Station|Chikuzen Oita Station]]. == External Links == * [http://www.daibu-hachiman.com/ 【公式】{{ill|Daibu Hachiman-gu|ja|大分八幡宮}]] * [http://www.kankou-iizuka.jp/homepage/sub.asp?id=90 【Daibu Hachiman-gu】 (Iizuka City website)] {{shinto-stub}} {{Normdaten}} ==Overview== ==References== * Plutschow, Herbe. ''Matsuri: The Festivals of Japan''. RoutledgeCurzon (1996) {{ISBN|1-873410-63-8}} * [[Richard Ponsonby-Fane|Ponsonby-Fane]], Richard Arthur Brabazon. (1959). [https://books.google.com/books?id=SLAeAAAAMAAJ&q=The+Imperial+House+of+Japan ''The Imperial House of Japan.''] Kyoto: Ponsonby Memorial Society. [http://www.worldcat.org/wcpa/oclc/194887 OCLC 194887] ==External links== {{commons category|Kono-jinja (Miyazu)}} *[https://www.motoise.jp Official home page] ==Notes== {{reflist}} {{Shinto shrine}} {{Munakata Faith}} {{Shinmei shrines}} {{Beppyo Shrines}} \ {{Ichinomiya}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Pages to be reviewed for curly bracket replacement error]] [[Category:Shrines in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:Buildings and structures in Miyazu City]] [[Category:History of Miyazu City]] [[Category:Meishin Taisha]] [[Category:Shikinai Taisha of Tango Province|名このしんしや]] [[Category:Ichinomiya]] [[Category:Kokuhēchūsha]] [[Category:National Treasures of Japan (Calligraphy, Documents, and Ancient Manuscripts)]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:Moto-Ise]] [[Category:Shinsei Taisha|社1]] [[Category:Japan Heritage]] [[Category:Pages that used to use Authority control]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Tango Province]] [[Category:Miyazu, Kyoto]] [[Category:Important Cultural Properties of Japan]] [[Category:National Treasures of Japan]] [[Category:Beppyo shrines]] [[Category:beppyo shinmei shrines needed to be moved in template]] [[Category:Myōjin Taisha]] [[Category:Kokuhei Chūsha]] [[Category:Moto-Ise shrines]] [[Category:Pages goodbye $1 Wikipedia 8]] [[Category:Kono Shrine]] [[Category:Moto-Geku Shrines]] [[Category:Munakata Faith]] [[Category:Expanded pages from Wikipedia]] }} [[sn:Kono Shrine]] [[en:Kono Shrine]] [[sn:ono Shrine]] [[sn: failed]]

{{Short description|Shinto shrine in Kyoto Prefecture, Japan}} {{Infobox religious building | name = Kono Jinja
籠神社 | image = Kono-jinja (Miyazu) haiden.JPG | caption = Haiden of Kono Jinja {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Kyoto Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|34|58.13|N|135|11|48.01|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Amenohoakari]] | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location =430 Ōgaki, Miyazu-shi, Kyoto-fu 629-2242 | website = {{Official|1=https://www.motoise.jp}} | architecture_style = ''Shinmei-zukuri'' | festival = April 24 | leadership = | designation1 = National Treasure of Japan | footnotes ={{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=pink|text align=center|[[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|Important Cultural Property]]}} }} [[File:Amabe Clan genealogy.jpg|right|thumb|Amabe clan genealogy]] {{nihongo|'''Kono Jinja'''|籠神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] in the Ōgaki neighborhood of the city of [[Miyazu, Kyoto|Miyazu]] in [[Kyoto Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of former [[Tango Province]]. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on April 24.The shrine is also called the {{nihongo|'''Moto-Ise Kono Jinja'''|元伊勢籠神社}}, and its ''[[kannushi]]'' has been in the Amabe clan since the [[Kofun period]].{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} It may be the [[Sōja shrine]] and [[Ichinomiya]] of the [[Tango Province]] ==Enshrined ''kami''== The primary ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Kono Jinja is: * {{nihongo|'''[[Amenohoakari]]'''|彦火明命 |}}, god of the sun and agriculture The secondary ''kami'' are: * {{nihongo|'''[[Toyoukebime]]'''|豊受大神|lt=Toyouke Ōmikami|1=Toyouke-hime}}, goddess of agriculture and industry * {{nihongo|'''[[Amaterasu]]'''|天照大神}}, goddess of the sun * {{nihongo|'''[[Watatsumi]]'''|海神}}, water deity * {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Ame-no-mikumari-no-kami|lt=Mikumari-no-Kami|sv|Mikumari-no-Kami|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-mikumari-no-kami|qq=}}'''|天水分神}} ==History== According to the legend of this shrine, Toyouke-Ōmikami was originally enshrined that this location before being relocated to the Outer Shrine of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]] during the reign of [[Emperor Yūryaku]] to offer sacred food to [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu Ōmikami]], the Sun Goddess. The shrine was originally called the {{nihongo|Manai Jinja|真名井神社||}}, but was renamed in 671 by the 26th generation ''kannushi'' to "Kagomiya" or "Kago Jinja" based on the tradition that the god of worship appeared in the snow in a basket. The main ''kami'' enshrined was changed to Amenohoakari in 719 by the 27th generation ''kannushi'', but Toyouke-Ōmikami retained as a secondary object of worship.The shrine and its rituals are described in both the ''[[Kojiki]]'' and the ''[[Nihon Shoki]]''. The shrine is listed in the ''[[Engishiki]]'' records from the early [[Heian period]], as a {{nihongo|''Myōjin Taisha''|名神大社||}} and the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of the province. It was located immediately to the west of the site of the Tango [[kokufu|provincial capital]].{{cite book |last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese}} The shrine consists of an upper and lower portion. The lower shrine is the [[Honden]] and is a ''[[Shinmei-zukuri]]'' structure with a cypress bark roof. It was rebuilt in 1845 and is designated as a Tangible Cultural Property of Kyoto Prefecture{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} During the [[Meiji period]] era of [[State Shinto]], the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 2nd Rank |国幣中社|[[kokuhei-chūsha]]}} under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines]]Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. (1959). ''The Imperial House of Japan,'' pp. 125. The shrine is located next to the [[Amanohashidate]]. ==Cultural Properties== ===NationalTreasures=== *{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図||}}, early [[Heian period]], it is considered the oldest family tree in Japan.The clan claims descent from Amenohoakari, and served as at the ''[[kuni no miyatsuko]]'' of [[Tanba Province]] before it was divided into Tamba and Tango.The document records 82 generations of descent from Amenohoakari. It was designated a National Treasure in 1972.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777|title=海部氏系図|trans-title=Amebe shikeizu|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 20, 2020}} ===National Important Cultural Properties=== *'''{{nihongo|Biane'''|扁額}}, wooden, [[Heian period]], inscribed "Kago no Daimyōjin", dated 976.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/5326|title=木造扁額|trans-title=Mokuzō hengaku|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 20, 2020}} *'''{{nihongo|[[Komainu]]'''|狛犬||}}, stone, [[Momoyama period]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/3741|title=石造狛犬|trans-title=Sekizōkomainu|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 20, 2020}} * '''{{nihongo|Excavated Items from Kono Jinja Kyozuka|丹後国府中籠神社経塚出土品|}}''', [[Heian period]], consisting of two copper cylinders, one mirror with a design of chrysanthemum, and mirror with a line drawing of a Buddha, dated 1188{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/9835|title=丹後国府中籠神社経塚出土品|trans-title=Tango kuni Fuchū kojinja Kyōdzuka shutsudo-hin|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 20, 2020}} ==Gallery== File:Kono-jinja (Miyazu) honden.JPG|Honden（Kyoto Prefectural ICP） File:Kono-jinja Miyazu3.JPG|Yamato ''Sazare-ishi'' File:Kono-jinja Miyazu Kyoto Pref04n3000.jpg|Koma-inu（ICP） File:Kono-jinja Miyazu Kyoto Pref05n3000.jpg|Koma-inu（ICP） File:Kono-jinja (Miyazu) shinmon.JPG|Gate File:Kono-jinja (Miyazu) torii.JPG|Ni-no-Torii ==See also== *[[List of Shinto shrines]] *[[List of National Treasures of Japan (ancient documents)]] *[[Ichinomiya]] {{神社 |名称 = {{ill|Kago Shrine|ja|籠神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kago Shrine|qq=}} |image = [[File:Kono-jinja (Miyazu) haiden.JPG|270px]]
Haiden |所在地 = {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ja|京都府|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyoto Prefecture|qq=}}{{ill|Miyazu City|ja|宮津市|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyazu City|qq=}}, Aza Ōgaki 430 |位置 = {{ウィキ座標2段度分秒|35|34|58.13|N|135|11|48.01|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} |祭神 = {{ill|Hikoakitsumeri no Mikoto|ja|彦火明命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hikoakitsumeri no Mikoto|qq=}} |神体 = |社格 = {{ill|Shikinai Taisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai Taisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} ({{ill|Meishin Taisha|ja|名神大|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meishin Taisha|qq=}})
{{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tango Province|qq=}}{{ill|Ichinomiya|ja|一宮|1=Ichinomiya|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichinomiya|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichinomiya|qq=}}
Former {{ill|Kokuhēchūsha|ja|国幣中社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokuhēchūsha|qq=}}
{{ill|Betsuhyō Jinja|ja|別表神社|1=Beppyo Shrine|2=ja|3=別表神社|4=simple|5=Beppyo shrine|6=zh|7=別表神社|8=mr|9=बेप्प्यो तीर्थ|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Betsuhyō Jinja|13=User:Immanuelle/Beppyo Shrine|qq=}} |創建 = Unknown (pre-history) |本殿 = {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|ja|神明造|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinmei-zukuri|qq=}} |別名 = {{ill|Moto-Ise Kago Shrine|ja|元伊勢籠神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Kago Shrine|qq=}}・{{ill|Naiku Moto-Miya|ja|内宮元宮|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Naiku Moto-Miya|qq=}}・{{ill|Komori Daikongen|ja|籠守大権現|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Komori Daikongen|qq=}} |札所等 = {{ill|Shinbutsu Reijōjunpai no Michi|ja|神仏霊場巡拝の道|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinbutsu Reijōjunpai no Michi|qq=}} No. 131 (Kyoto No. 51) |例祭 = {{ill|April 24 (Aoi-sai)|ja|4月24日（葵祭）|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/April 24 (Aoi-sai)|qq=}} |神事 = |地図 = {{Location map|Japan Kyoto|label={{ill|Kago Shrine|ja|籠神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kago Shrine|qq=}}|position=top|width=200|float=center|caption=|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=20}}{{maplink2|frame=yes|plain=yes|type=point|zoom=11|marker=religious-shinto|frame-align=center|frame-width=200}} }} {{GeoGroup}} [[File:Precincts of Kono-jinja.JPG|thumb|{{center|View of the precincts (from {{ill|Kasamatsu Park|ja|傘松公園|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasamatsu Park|qq=}})}}{{small|Shrine buildings visible at lower left, and {{ill|Amanohashidate|ja|天橋立|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amanohashidate|qq=}} at upper right.}}]] [[File:Kono-jinja (Miyazu) otorii.JPG|thumb|{{center|First Torii}}]] '''Kago Shrine''' (read “Kono-jinja” – also sometimes read “Komori-jinja,” though the reading “Kono-jinja” is used here) is a Shinto shrine located in Ōgaki, [[Miyazu City]], [[Kyoto Prefecture]]. It is classified as a Shikinai Taisha (Meishin Taisha) and the Ichinomiya of Tango Province. Its former shrine Ranking under the modern system was that of a Kokuhēchūsha, and it is now one of the Betsuhyō Jinja under the Association of Shinto Shrines. It is also one of the shrines of Moto-Ise, and is known by various names such as “Moto-Ise Kago Shrine,” “Naiku Moto-Miya,” “Komori Daikongen,” and “Kago Daimyōjin.” The shrine’s head priest has been hereditary in the {{ill|Amabe Clan|ja|海部氏|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amabe Clan|qq=}}. Although the origin of the Sōsha of Tango Province is unknown, one theory holds that this shrine also served as the Sōsha. In April 2017 (Heisei 29), the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology recognized it as one of the cultural properties that help tell the story of Japan’s cultural heritage – as part of the “Japan Heritage” story "Tango Chirimen Corridor."{{Cite web|和書|author=文化庁|authorlink=文化庁|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/nihon_isan/pdf/nihon_isan_pamphlet_2019.pdf|title=日本遺産認定ストーリー一覧|accessdate=2020-11-11}}{{Cite web|和書|author=文化庁|authorlink=文化庁|url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story043/index.html|title=300th year を紡ぐ絹が織り成す丹後ちりめん回廊|website=日本遺産ポータルサイト|accessdate=2020-11-11}} == Enshrined Deities == The deities enshrined at Kago Shrine consist of five figures. '''Principal Deity''' * '''{{ill|Hikoakitsumeri no Mikoto|ja|彦火明命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hikoakitsumeri no Mikoto|qq=}}''' (Hikoakitsumeri no Mikoto) **Also referred to as {{ill|Amatenohikohikari no Mikoto|ja|天火明命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amatenohikohikari no Mikoto|qq=}}, {{ill|Amaterasu Mitama no Kami|ja|天照御魂神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Mitama no Kami|qq=}}, or {{ill|Amaterasu Kuniteru Hikoakitsumeri no Mikoto|ja|天照国照彦火明命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu Kuniteru Hikoakitsumeri no Mikoto|qq=}}, as well as {{ill|Nigihayahi|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=}}; considered the ancestral deity of the Amabe clan. '''Associated Deities''' * {{ill|Toyouke-no-Ōkami|ja|豊受大神|lt=Toyouke Ōmikami|1=Toyouke-hime|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke-no-Ōkami|13=User:Immanuelle/Toyouke-hime|qq=}} – also known as “Goshizunushi,” * {{ill|Amaterasu-Ōkami|ja|天照大神|1=Amaterasu|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu-Ōkami|13=User:Immanuelle/Amaterasu|qq=}} * {{ill|Watatsumi|ja|海神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Watatsumi|qq=}} – the tutelary deity of the Amabe clan. * {{ill|Ame-no-Mikumari no Kami|ja|天水分神|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Mikumari no Kami|qq=}} Various theories exist regarding these enshrined deities.{{ill|Japanese Deities|ja|日本の神々|1=Kamigami|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Japanese Deities|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamigami|qq=}} – Kago Shrine entry. According to the "Tango-koku Shikishōjō Jikkō," {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qq=}} is cited,Based on a tradition from an excerpt of the "Tango-koku Fudoki" (as included in the Shaku Nihonki). while the "Shinja Meisaichō" lists Ame-no-Mikumari as the deity. == History == Kago Shrine was founded in the 3rd year of {{ill|Shinkame|ja|神亀|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinkame|qq=}} (726) during the Nara period. According to shrine tradition, the site is the place where {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Empress Jingū|qq=}} temporarily stayed on her return journey from the conquest of the Three Kingdoms. According to the "Hakozaki Shrine Engi" (a record from {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|ja|石清水八幡宮|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwashimizu Hachimangū|qq=}}), in the 21st year of {{ill|Engi|ja|延喜|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi|qq=}} (921) an oracle was received regarding the relocation to Hakozaki-hama (the present-day Hakozaki area of Higashi Ward in [[Fukuoka City]]); then in the 1st year of {{ill|Enchō|ja|延長|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enchō|qq=}} (923) the shrine was relocated, marking the beginning of Hakozaki Shrine. The oracle for Hakozaki Shrine was drawn from the oracle collection of Usa Jingu, the origin story of the Hachiman deities, which states, "Either I, from Usa Jingu, or the Hon-miya of Honami Oita is my main shrine." Even after relocating to Hakozaki Shrine, it continued to be fervently venerated as the head branch (第一社) among the Five Hachiman Shrines of Kyushu. Nearby, there are ruins of an ancient temple and the remains of the "Daibu Haiji" pagoda. At the time of its founding, the shrine buildings were located on a hillside behind the present site, but during the Sengoku period they were burned down in warfare. In the 5th year of {{ill|Tenshō|ja|天正|1=Tenshō (Momoyama period)|lt=Tenshō Era|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenshō|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenshō (Momoyama period)|qq=}} (1577), {{ill|Akizuki Tanemi|ja|秋月種実|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akizuki Tanemi|qq=}} rebuilt the shrine at the current location. In 1872 (Meiji 5), it was classified as a Gōsha under the modern shrine Ranking system. In 1995 (Heisei 7), a major restoration was carried out. == Facilities == [[File:Pond in Daibu Hachiman Shrine.jpg|thumb|250px|Hojo Pond]] [[File:Grand camphor tree in Daibu Hachiman Shrine.jpg|thumb|250px|Great Camphor Tree]] * Haiden (Worship Hall) * Honden (Main Hall) **Both the Haiden and Honden were extensively repaired in Heisei 7 (1995). * Shimon (Divine Gate) * Hojo Pond – a pond used during the Hojo Festival. * The Well of Emperor Ōjin’s Birth Water * Great Camphor Tree – an estimated 350‑year‑old camphor tree ({{ill|Kusunoki|ja|クスノキ|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki|qq=}}) designated as a Natural Monument of Fukuoka Prefecture. According to tradition, it is said to be a descendant of the tree that {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Empress Jingū|qq=}} brought back from the Korean Peninsula. * Uguisuzuka – a hill approximately 10 meters high located on a detached part of the grounds near [[Chikuzen Oita Station]] on JR; according to tradition, Empress Jingū disbanded her troops here, and it is said that the place name “Oita” originated from this event. == Annual Festival == At the annual festival (Hojo-kai) held each September, the “Daibu Lion Dance” is performed. This lion dance is designated as an Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Fukuoka Prefecture. It is said to have been transmitted from {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|ja|石清水八幡宮|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwashimizu Hachimangū|qq=}} during the Edo period (specifically in Kyōhō 9, 1724) and, together with the “Earth-worker Lion Dance” from Hakata (in {{ill|Kaho District|ja|嘉穂郡|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaho District|qq=}}, {{ill|Katsugawa Town|ja|桂川町|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katsugawa Town|qq=}}), has influenced lion dances in southern Fukuoka. It is also noted that, perhaps due to transmission from Kyoto, the accompanying festival music and shouts have a nuance similar to Kyoto dialect. == Access == * Approximately a 15‑minute walk from [[JR Kyushu]]’s {{ill|Fukuhoku Yutaka Line|ja|福北ゆたか線|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuhoku Yutaka Line|qq=}} [[Chikuzen Oita Station|Chikuzen Oita Station]]. == External Links == * [http://www.daibu-hachiman.com/ 【公式】{{ill|Daibu Hachiman-gu|ja|大分八幡宮}]] * [http://www.kankou-iizuka.jp/homepage/sub.asp?id=90 【Daibu Hachiman-gu】 (Iizuka City website)] {{shinto-stub}} {{Normdaten}} ==Overview== ==References== * Plutschow, Herbe. 籠神社 | image = Kono-jinja (Miyazu) haiden.JPG | caption = Haiden of Kono Jinja {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Kyoto Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|34|58.13|N|135|11|48.01|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Amenohoakari]] | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location =430 Ōgaki, Miyazu-shi, Kyoto-fu 629-2242 | website = {{Official|1=https://www.motoise.jp}} | architecture_style = ''Shinmei-zukuri'' | festival = April 24 | leadership = | designation1 = National Treasure of Japan | footnotes ={{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=pink|text align=center|[[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|Important Cultural Property]]}} }} [[File:Amabe Clan genealogy.jpg|right|thumb|Amabe clan genealogy]] {{nihongo|'''Kono Jinja'''|籠神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] in the Ōgaki neighborhood of the city of [[Miyazu, Kyoto|Miyazu]] in [[Kyoto Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of former [[Tango Province]]. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on April 24.The shrine is also called the {{nihongo|'''Moto-Ise Kono Jinja'''|元伊勢籠神社}}, and its ''[[kannushi]]'' has been in the Amabe clan since the [[Kofun period]].{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} It may be the [[Sōja shrine]] and [[Ichinomiya]] of the [[Tango Province]] ==Enshrined ''kami''== The primary ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Kono Jinja is: * {{nihongo|'''[[Amenohoakari]]'''|彦火明命 |}}, god of the sun and agriculture The secondary ''kami'' are: * {{nihongo|'''[[Toyoukebime]]'''|豊受大神|lt=Toyouke Ōmikami|1=Toyouke-hime}}, goddess of agriculture and industry * {{nihongo|'''[[Amaterasu]]'''|天照大神}}, goddess of the sun * {{nihongo|'''[[Watatsumi]]'''|海神}}, water deity * {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Ame-no-mikumari-no-kami|lt=Mikumari-no-Kami|sv|Mikumari-no-Kami|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-mikumari-no-kami|qq=}}'''|天水分神}} ==History== According to the legend of this shrine, Toyouke-Ōmikami was originally enshrined that this location before being relocated to the Outer Shrine of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]] during the reign of [[Emperor Yūryaku]] to offer sacred food to [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu Ōmikami]], the Sun Goddess. The shrine was originally called the {{nihongo|Manai Jinja|真名井神社||}}, but was renamed in 671 by the 26th generation ''kannushi'' to "Kagomiya" or "Kago Jinja" based on the tradition that the god of worship appeared in the snow in a basket. The main ''kami'' enshrined was changed to Amenohoakari in 719 by the 27th generation ''kannushi'', but Toyouke-Ōmikami retained as a secondary object of worship.The shrine and its rituals are described in both the ''[[Kojiki]]'' and the ''[[Nihon Shoki]]''. The shrine is listed in the ''[[Engishiki]]'' records from the early [[Heian period]], as a {{nihongo|''Myōjin Taisha''|名神大社||}} and the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of the province. It was located immediately to the west of the site of the Tango [[kokufu|provincial capital]].{{cite book |last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese}} The shrine consists of an upper and lower portion. The lower shrine is the [[Honden]] and is a ''[[Shinmei-zukuri]]'' structure with a cypress bark roof. It was rebuilt in 1845 and is designated as a Tangible Cultural Property of Kyoto Prefecture{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} During the [[Meiji period]] era of [[State Shinto]], the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 2nd Rank |国幣中社|[[kokuhei-chūsha]]}} under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines]]Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. (1959). ''The Imperial House of Japan,'' pp. 125. The shrine is located next to the [[Amanohashidate]]. ==Cultural Properties== ===NationalTreasures=== *{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図||}}, early [[Heian period]], it is considered the oldest family tree in Japan.The clan claims descent from Amenohoakari, and served as at the ''[[kuni no miyatsuko]]'' of [[Tanba Province]] before it was divided into Tamba and Tango.The document records 82 generations of descent from Amenohoakari. It was designated a National Treasure in 1972.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777|title=海部氏系図|trans-title=Amebe shikeizu|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 20, 2020}} ===National Important Cultural Properties=== *'''{{nihongo|Biane'''|扁額}}, wooden, [[Heian period]], inscribed "Kago no Daimyōjin", dated 976.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/5326|title=木造扁額|trans-title=Mokuzō hengaku|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 20, 2020}} *'''{{nihongo|[[Komainu]]'''|狛犬||}}, stone, [[Momoyama period]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/3741|title=石造狛犬|trans-title=Sekizōkomainu|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 20, 2020}} * '''{{nihongo|Excavated Items from Kono Jinja Kyozuka|丹後国府中籠神社経塚出土品|}}''', [[Heian period]], consisting of two copper cylinders, one mirror with a design of chrysanthemum, and mirror with a line drawing of a Buddha, dated 1188{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/9835|title=丹後国府中籠神社経塚出土品|trans-title=Tango kuni Fuchū kojinja Kyōdzuka shutsudo-hin|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 20, 2020}} ==Gallery== File:Kono-jinja (Miyazu) honden.JPG|Honden（Kyoto Prefectural ICP） File:Kono-jinja Miyazu3.JPG|Yamato ''Sazare-ishi'' File:Kono-jinja Miyazu Kyoto Pref04n3000.jpg|Koma-inu（ICP） File:Kono-jinja Miyazu Kyoto Pref05n3000.jpg|Koma-inu（ICP） File:Kono-jinja (Miyazu) shinmon.JPG|Gate File:Kono-jinja (Miyazu) torii.JPG|Ni-no-Torii ==See also== *[[List of Shinto shrines]] *[[List of National Treasures of Japan (ancient documents)]] *[[Ichinomiya]] {{神社 |名称 = {{ill|Kago Shrine|ja|籠神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kago Shrine|qq=}} |image = [[File:Kono-jinja (Miyazu) haiden.JPG|270px]]

It is classified as a Shikinai Taisha (Meishin Taisha) and the Ichinomiya of Tango Province. Its former shrine Ranking under the modern system was that of a Kokuhēchūsha, and it is now one of the Betsuhyō Jinja under the Association of Shinto Shrines. It is also one of the shrines of Moto-Ise, and is known by various names such as “Moto-Ise Kago Shrine,” “Naiku Moto-Miya,” “Komori Daikongen,” and “Kago Daimyōjin.” The shrine’s head priest has been hereditary in the {{ill|Amabe Clan|ja|海部氏|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amabe Clan|qq=}}. Although the origin of the Sōsha of Tango Province is unknown, one theory holds that this shrine also served as the Sōsha. In April 2017 (Heisei 29), the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology recognized it as one of the cultural properties that help tell the story of Japan’s cultural heritage – as part of the “Japan Heritage” story "Tango Chirimen Corridor."{{Cite web|和書|author=文化庁|authorlink=文化庁|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/nihon_isan/pdf/nihon_isan_pamphlet_2019.pdf|title=日本遺産認定ストーリー一覧|accessdate=2020-11-11}}{{Cite web|和書|author=文化庁|authorlink=文化庁|url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story043/index.html|title=300th year を紡ぐ絹が織り成す丹後ちりめん回廊|website=日本遺産ポータルサイト|accessdate=2020-11-11}} == Enshrined Deities == The deities enshrined at Kago Shrine consist of five figures. According to the "Tango-koku Shikishōjō Jikkō," {{ill|Izanagi|ja|伊弉諾尊|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izanagi|qq=}} is cited,Based on a tradition from an excerpt of the "Tango-koku Fudoki" (as included in the Shaku Nihonki). while the "Shinja Meisaichō" lists Ame-no-Mikumari as the deity. == History == Kago Shrine was founded in the 3rd year of {{ill|Shinkame|ja|神亀|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinkame|qq=}} (726) during the Nara period. According to shrine tradition, the site is the place where {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Empress Jingū|qq=}} temporarily stayed on her return journey from the conquest of the Three Kingdoms. According to the "Hakozaki Shrine Engi" (a record from {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|ja|石清水八幡宮|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwashimizu Hachimangū|qq=}}), in the 21st year of {{ill|Engi|ja|延喜|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engi|qq=}} (921) an oracle was received regarding the relocation to Hakozaki-hama (the present-day Hakozaki area of Higashi Ward in [[Fukuoka City]]); then in the 1st year of {{ill|Enchō|ja|延長|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enchō|qq=}} (923) the shrine was relocated, marking the beginning of Hakozaki Shrine. The oracle for Hakozaki Shrine was drawn from the oracle collection of Usa Jingu, the origin story of the Hachiman deities, which states, "Either I, from Usa Jingu, or the Hon-miya of Honami Oita is my main shrine." Even after relocating to Hakozaki Shrine, it continued to be fervently venerated as the head branch (第一社) among the Five Hachiman Shrines of Kyushu. Nearby, there are ruins of an ancient temple and the remains of the "Daibu Haiji" pagoda. At the time of its founding, the shrine buildings were located on a hillside behind the present site, but during the Sengoku period they were burned down in warfare. In the 5th year of {{ill|Tenshō|ja|天正|1=Tenshō (Momoyama period)|lt=Tenshō Era|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenshō|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenshō (Momoyama period)|qq=}} (1577), {{ill|Akizuki Tanemi|ja|秋月種実|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akizuki Tanemi|qq=}} rebuilt the shrine at the current location. In 1872 (Meiji 5), it was classified as a Gōsha under the modern shrine Ranking system. In 1995 (Heisei 7), a major restoration was carried out. == Facilities == [[File:Pond in Daibu Hachiman Shrine.jpg|thumb|250px|Hojo Pond]] [[File:Grand camphor tree in Daibu Hachiman Shrine.jpg|thumb|250px|Great Camphor Tree]] * Haiden (Worship Hall) * Honden (Main Hall) **Both the Haiden and Honden were extensively repaired in Heisei 7 (1995). * Shimon (Divine Gate) * Hojo Pond – a pond used during the Hojo Festival. * The Well of Emperor Ōjin’s Birth Water * Great Camphor Tree – an estimated 350‑year‑old camphor tree ({{ill|Kusunoki|ja|クスノキ|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki|qq=}}) designated as a Natural Monument of Fukuoka Prefecture. According to tradition, it is said to be a descendant of the tree that {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Empress Jingū|qq=}} brought back from the Korean Peninsula. * Uguisuzuka – a hill approximately 10 meters high located on a detached part of the grounds near [[Chikuzen Oita Station]] on JR; according to tradition, Empress Jingū disbanded her troops here, and it is said that the place name “Oita” originated from this event. == Annual Festival == At the annual festival (Hojo-kai) held each September, the “Daibu Lion Dance” is performed. This lion dance is designated as an Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Fukuoka Prefecture. It is said to have been transmitted from {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|ja|石清水八幡宮|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwashimizu Hachimangū|qq=}} during the Edo period (specifically in Kyōhō 9, 1724) and, together with the “Earth-worker Lion Dance” from Hakata (in {{ill|Kaho District|ja|嘉穂郡|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaho District|qq=}}, {{ill|Katsugawa Town|ja|桂川町|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katsugawa Town|qq=}}), has influenced lion dances in southern Fukuoka. It is also noted that, perhaps due to transmission from Kyoto, the accompanying festival music and shouts have a nuance similar to Kyoto dialect. == Access == * Approximately a 15‑minute walk from [[JR Kyushu]]’s {{ill|Fukuhoku Yutaka Line|ja|福北ゆたか線|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuhoku Yutaka Line|qq=}} [[Chikuzen Oita Station|Chikuzen Oita Station]]. == External Links == * [http://www.daibu-hachiman.com/ 【公式】{{ill|Daibu Hachiman-gu|ja|大分八幡宮}]] * [http://www.kankou-iizuka.jp/homepage/sub.asp?id=90 【Daibu Hachiman-gu】 (Iizuka City website)] {{shinto-stub}} {{Normdaten}} ==Overview== ==References== * Plutschow, Herbe. 籠神社 | image = Kono-jinja (Miyazu) haiden.JPG | caption = Haiden of Kono Jinja {{Infobox mapframe|tyep=shape|zoom=14|frame-width=240}} | map_type = Japan Kyoto Prefecture#Japan | map_alt = | coordinates = {{coord|35|34|58.13|N|135|11|48.01|E|region:JP-26_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} | map_relief = 1 | map_size = | map_caption = | religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | type = | deity = [[Amenohoakari]] | founded_by = | established = | date_destroyed = | location =430 Ōgaki, Miyazu-shi, Kyoto-fu 629-2242 | website = {{Official|1=https://www.motoise.jp}} | architecture_style = ''Shinmei-zukuri'' | festival = April 24 | leadership = | designation1 = National Treasure of Japan | footnotes ={{box|background=white|align=center|wide=yes|border size=3px|border color=pink|text align=center|[[Important Cultural Properties of Japan|Important Cultural Property]]}} }} [[File:Amabe Clan genealogy.jpg|right|thumb|Amabe clan genealogy]] {{nihongo|'''Kono Jinja'''|籠神社}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] in the Ōgaki neighborhood of the city of [[Miyazu, Kyoto|Miyazu]] in [[Kyoto Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. It is the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of former [[Tango Province]]. The main festival of the shrine is held annually on April 24.The shrine is also called the {{nihongo|'''Moto-Ise Kono Jinja'''|元伊勢籠神社}}, and its ''[[kannushi]]'' has been in the Amabe clan since the [[Kofun period]].{{cite book |last1=Shibuya |first1=Nobuhiro |title=Shokoku jinja Ichinomiya Ninomiya San'nomiya |date=2015 |publisher= Yamakawa shuppansha |isbn=978-4634150867 |language=Japanese}} It may be the [[Sōja shrine]] and [[Ichinomiya]] of the [[Tango Province]] ==Enshrined ''kami''== The primary ''[[kami]]'' enshrined at Kono Jinja is: * {{nihongo|'''[[Amenohoakari]]'''|彦火明命 |}}, god of the sun and agriculture The secondary ''kami'' are: * {{nihongo|'''[[Toyoukebime]]'''|豊受大神|lt=Toyouke Ōmikami|1=Toyouke-hime}}, goddess of agriculture and industry * {{nihongo|'''[[Amaterasu]]'''|天照大神}}, goddess of the sun * {{nihongo|'''[[Watatsumi]]'''|海神}}, water deity * {{nihongo|'''{{ill|Ame-no-mikumari-no-kami|lt=Mikumari-no-Kami|sv|Mikumari-no-Kami|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-mikumari-no-kami|qq=}}'''|天水分神}} ==History== According to the legend of this shrine, Toyouke-Ōmikami was originally enshrined that this location before being relocated to the Outer Shrine of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]] during the reign of [[Emperor Yūryaku]] to offer sacred food to [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu Ōmikami]], the Sun Goddess. The shrine was originally called the {{nihongo|Manai Jinja|真名井神社||}}, but was renamed in 671 by the 26th generation ''kannushi'' to "Kagomiya" or "Kago Jinja" based on the tradition that the god of worship appeared in the snow in a basket. The main ''kami'' enshrined was changed to Amenohoakari in 719 by the 27th generation ''kannushi'', but Toyouke-Ōmikami retained as a secondary object of worship.The shrine and its rituals are described in both the ''[[Kojiki]]'' and the ''[[Nihon Shoki]]''. The shrine is listed in the ''[[Engishiki]]'' records from the early [[Heian period]], as a {{nihongo|''Myōjin Taisha''|名神大社||}} and the ''[[ichinomiya]]'' of the province. It was located immediately to the west of the site of the Tango [[kokufu|provincial capital]].{{cite book |last1=Yoshiki |first1=Emi |title=Zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' tettei gaido |date=2007 |publisher=PHP Institute |isbn=978-4569669304 |language=Japanese}} The shrine consists of an upper and lower portion. The lower shrine is the [[Honden]] and is a ''[[Shinmei-zukuri]]'' structure with a cypress bark roof. It was rebuilt in 1845 and is designated as a Tangible Cultural Property of Kyoto Prefecture{{cite book |last1=Okada |first1=Shoji |title=Taiyō no chizuchō 24 zenkoku 'Ichinomiya' meguri |date=2014 |publisher=Heibonsha |isbn=978-4582945614 |language=Japanese}} During the [[Meiji period]] era of [[State Shinto]], the shrine was designated as a {{nihongo|National shrine, 2nd Rank |国幣中社|[[kokuhei-chūsha]]}} under the [[Modern system of Ranked Shinto Shrines]]Ponsonby-Fane, Richard. (1959). ''The Imperial House of Japan,'' pp. 125. The shrine is located next to the [[Amanohashidate]]. ==Cultural Properties== ===NationalTreasures=== *{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図||}}, early [[Heian period]], it is considered the oldest family tree in Japan.The clan claims descent from Amenohoakari, and served as at the ''[[kuni no miyatsuko]]'' of [[Tanba Province]] before it was divided into Tamba and Tango.The document records 82 generations of descent from Amenohoakari. It was designated a National Treasure in 1972.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777|title=海部氏系図|trans-title=Amebe shikeizu|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 20, 2020}} ===National Important Cultural Properties=== *'''{{nihongo|Biane'''|扁額}}, wooden, [[Heian period]], inscribed "Kago no Daimyōjin", dated 976.{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/5326|title=木造扁額|trans-title=Mokuzō hengaku|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 20, 2020}} *'''{{nihongo|[[Komainu]]'''|狛犬||}}, stone, [[Momoyama period]].{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/3741|title=石造狛犬|trans-title=Sekizōkomainu|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 20, 2020}} * '''{{nihongo|Excavated Items from Kono Jinja Kyozuka|丹後国府中籠神社経塚出土品|}}''', [[Heian period]], consisting of two copper cylinders, one mirror with a design of chrysanthemum, and mirror with a line drawing of a Buddha, dated 1188{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/9835|title=丹後国府中籠神社経塚出土品|trans-title=Tango kuni Fuchū kojinja Kyōdzuka shutsudo-hin|language=Japanese |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |accessdate=August 20, 2020}} ==Gallery== File:Kono-jinja (Miyazu) honden.JPG|Honden（Kyoto Prefectural ICP） File:Kono-jinja Miyazu3.JPG|Yamato ''Sazare-ishi'' File:Kono-jinja Miyazu Kyoto Pref04n3000.jpg|Koma-inu（ICP） File:Kono-jinja Miyazu Kyoto Pref05n3000.jpg|Koma-inu（ICP） File:Kono-jinja (Miyazu) shinmon.JPG|Gate File:Kono-jinja (Miyazu) torii.JPG|Ni-no-Torii ==See also== *[[List of Shinto shrines]] *[[List of National Treasures of Japan (ancient documents)]] *[[Ichinomiya]] {{神社 |名称 = {{ill|Kago Shrine|ja|籠神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kago Shrine|qq=}} |image = [[File:Kono-jinja (Miyazu) haiden.JPG|270px]]

It is classified as a Shikinai Taisha (Meishin Taisha) and the Ichinomiya of Tango Province. Its former shrine Ranking under the modern system was that of a Kokuhēchūsha, and it is now one of the Betsuhyō Jinja under the Association of Shinto Shrines. It is also one of the shrines of Moto-Ise, and is known by various names such as “Moto-Ise Kago Shrine,” “Naiku Moto-Miya,” “Komori Daikongen,” and “Kago Daimyōjin.” The shrine’s head priest has been hereditary in the {{ill|Amabe Clan|ja|海部氏|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Amabe Clan|qq=}}. Although the origin of the Sōsha of Tango Province is unknown, one theory holds that this shrine also served as the Sōsha. In April 2017 (Heisei 29), the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology recognized it as one of the cultural properties that help tell the story of Japan’s cultural heritage – as part of the “Japan Heritage” story "Tango Chirimen Corridor."{{Cite web|和書|author=文化庁|authorlink=文化庁|url=https://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/nihon_isan/pdf/nihon_isan_pamphlet_2019.pdf|title=日本遺産認定ストーリー一覧|accessdate=2020-11-11}}{{Cite web|和書|author=文化庁|authorlink=文化庁|url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story043/index.html|title=300th year を紡ぐ絹が織り成す丹後ちりめん回廊|website=日本遺産ポータルサイト|accessdate=2020-11-11}} == Enshrined Deities == The deities enshrined at Kago Shrine consist of five figures. In 1872 (Meiji 5), it was classified as a Gōsha under the modern shrine Ranking system. In 1995 (Heisei 7), a major restoration was carried out. == Facilities == [[File:Pond in Daibu Hachiman Shrine.jpg|thumb|250px|Hojo Pond]] [[File:Grand camphor tree in Daibu Hachiman Shrine.jpg|thumb|250px|Great Camphor Tree]] * Haiden (Worship Hall) * Honden (Main Hall) **Both the Haiden and Honden were extensively repaired in Heisei 7 (1995). * Shimon (Divine Gate) * Hojo Pond – a pond used during the Hojo Festival. * The Well of Emperor Ōjin’s Birth Water * Great Camphor Tree – an estimated 350‑year‑old camphor tree ({{ill|Kusunoki|ja|クスノキ|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kusunoki|qq=}}) designated as a Natural Monument of Fukuoka Prefecture. According to tradition, it is said to be a descendant of the tree that {{ill|Empress Jingū|ja|神功皇后|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Empress Jingū|qq=}} brought back from the Korean Peninsula. * Uguisuzuka – a hill approximately 10 meters high located on a detached part of the grounds near [[Chikuzen Oita Station]] on JR; according to tradition, Empress Jingū disbanded her troops here, and it is said that the place name “Oita” originated from this event. == Annual Festival == At the annual festival (Hojo-kai) held each September, the “Daibu Lion Dance” is performed. This lion dance is designated as an Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Fukuoka Prefecture. It is said to have been transmitted from {{ill|Iwashimizu Hachimangū|ja|石清水八幡宮|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwashimizu Hachimangū|qq=}} during the Edo period (specifically in Kyōhō 9, 1724) and, together with the “Earth-worker Lion Dance” from Hakata (in {{ill|Kaho District|ja|嘉穂郡|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaho District|qq=}}, {{ill|Katsugawa Town|ja|桂川町|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katsugawa Town|qq=}}), has influenced lion dances in southern Fukuoka. It is also noted that, perhaps due to transmission from Kyoto, the accompanying festival music and shouts have a nuance similar to Kyoto dialect. == Access == * Approximately a 15‑minute walk from [[JR Kyushu]]’s {{ill|Fukuhoku Yutaka Line|ja|福北ゆたか線|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukuhoku Yutaka Line|qq=}} [[Chikuzen Oita Station|Chikuzen Oita Station]]. == External Links == * [http://www.daibu-hachiman.com/ 【公式】{{ill|Daibu Hachiman-gu|ja|大分八幡宮}]] * [http://www.kankou-iizuka.jp/homepage/sub.asp?id=90 【Daibu Hachiman-gu】 (Iizuka City website)] {{shinto-stub}} {{Normdaten}} ==Overview== ==References== * Plutschow, Herbe.
